html-in-canvas

Web·by @rpavlini·2026-08-19·inspora page·original post

What it is

html-in-canvas: a 'Coming soon' shop teaser rendered in canvas - a pile of hand-drawn sticker/stamp artwork ('1779 CASEMATES SQUARE', 'LY BATTERY SURVIVORS CLUB', 'Lo-Fi', 'GIBRALTAR') sits center page and a large glass sphere acts as a draggable magnifying lens: it refracts and enlarges whatever artwork passes beneath it with chromatic rim fringes; copy: 'Meanwhile, click, drag and explore'; light and dark page variants.

Media

Frame-by-frame

0-20%
Sphere parked over the sticker pile; artwork inside it bulges enlarged with rainbow dispersion at the glass rim.
20-50%
Sphere drags left/right across the pile: stamps warp and swell through the lens, sizes distorting with barrel refraction.
50-75%
Sphere rests on the 'Lo-Fi' sticker - script lettering hugely magnified, rim fringe visible; surrounding pile static.
75-100%
Dark-mode variant of the same comp; sphere picks up environment tint; settings panel (controls) visible at right in dark frames.

Build prompt

Build a canvas magnifier hero. White (or near-black) page, centered 'Coming soon' 28px with 'Meanwhile, click, drag and explore ↓' subline. Below, a ~700x300 canvas holding a scattered pile of 8-10 sticker illustrations (stamp-bordered prints, badges, script lettering), each pre-rendered with slight rotation. Overlay a 180px glass sphere the user drags: render with a refraction shader - sample the scene texture through a sphere-normal offset (fisheye/barrel, ~1.6x center magnification easing to 0 at rim), add chromatic dispersion (sample RGB at 1.00/1.02/1.04 radial scales) for rainbow rim fringes, plus a specular highlight top-left and faint fresnel rim. Physics: sphere follows pointer 1:1 while dragging, on release glides with velocity decay and soft-collides with canvas edges. WebGL (three.js custom shader or raw canvas2d drawImage slices as fallback). Dark mode: invert page, tint sphere white/10.
